model.description: NAME THE FAMILY, not the instance (PO ruling on the R40.39 audit): fixing only `feature` leaves TestCase corpus-walking tomorrow. Every ior:class unit type must EITHER have a TYPE-INDEX link folder (scenario/sprints.md/<type>/) OR be EXPLICITLY DECLARED alt-indexed (scenario/alt/, by-value — Company/Email/Phone) or singleton (index-over-one-unit pointless — Config) — DECLARED, never DEFAULTED to a corpus scan. A NEW unit type CANNOT be introduced without such a declaration. This is the difference between fixing a bug (R40.39: feature+TestCase) and closing a class: index-by-default-to-corpus-scan is the disease; feature and TestCase were two symptoms.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every ior:class unit type IN USE is DECLARED in a registry as EXACTLY ONE of: type-indexed (scenario/sprints.md/<type>/ ln folder), alt-indexed (scenario/alt/<type>/ by-value), or singleton — DECLARED, never DEFAULTED. NO type resolves by a corpus-scan-because-unclassified.

A NEW unit type CANNOT be introduced without an index/alt/singleton declaration — by construction: the loader/resolver REFUSES an undeclared type (fail-loud) rather than silently falling back to a corpus scan. Adding a type = adding its declaration, or it does not load.

A GATE FAILS if ANY ior:class type in use lacks a declaration (index OR alt OR singleton), with STUB-MUST-FAIL: introduce an undeclared type (or drop a declaration) -> assert RED. Closes the class by construction, so the next missing index is caught at the gate, not the next incident.

The 11 currently-unindexed types are CLASSIFIED + resolved: GENUINE (Feature, TestCase -> type-index per R40.39); ALT-INDEXED (Company/Email/Phone -> declare, verified scenario/alt/); SINGLETON (Config -> declare); and Profile/WebItem/Gate/ModelElement/Relationship classified genuine-vs-intentional by architect ruling. No type left in the default-corpus-scan bucket.
